1.point: The three worlds (matter, images, intellects) are one world at three depths, each sampled by a faculty we already have, so the dead have gone deeper, not away.
steps: The soul is a microcosm, so each knowing faculty samples one world
Senses sample the material world; the other two are unseen, not distant
Imagination samples a world of shape and colour without matter
That world of images exists in its own right and is where the dead enter
Intellect samples a world of pure meaning, the world of intellects
The world of images stands between the two, hence 'middle' and barzakh
The worlds are dimensions of this one, nested in depth not distance
So the dead have passed deeper into this world, not elsewhere

2.point: The soul belongs to all three worlds and slips into the middle one whenever its grip on the body loosens (sleep, death, contemplation); unlike an angel it has no fixed rank, so its reach depends on how it lives.
steps: The soul is the intermediary between spirit and clay, so it has a share in each world
Its attention is held by the body; that hold loosens at three times
Sleep: attention loosens, the soul touches the middle world (predictive dreams)
Death: the Qur'an pairs it with sleep; the difference is degree, and the soul goes on in an image body
Contemplation (muraqaba): the same loosening achieved awake by turning attention to God
Angels have fixed stations; the soul can move, so how far it goes is left open

3.point: The image body is shaped by deeds the way habits shape character; what the soul meets after death is largely its own deeds made visible, and that shaping is happening now.
steps: Objection: if everyone passes over anyway, conduct seems not to matter
Repeated acts shape the self (habit of lying)
The image body is far more sensitive than the physical one: sin deforms it, piety makes it shine
Authority that a second, invisible form is fixed by the soul's qualities and state
Scripture: the light of the faithful is their own; reward and punishment are the deeds themselves made manifest
So the form the soul meets is its own deeds made visible, and it is being made today

4.point: There is one nafs that is called commanding, self-blaming or at peace according to its state; it can move between them, remembrance, fasting and night prayer move it, and whatever it becomes stays with us, so its final state is in our hands.
steps: If deeds shape the soul, the self is not fixed; the Qur'an names three states
The commanding self: bodily side rules the spiritual
The self-blaming self: remorse after giving in, a hopeful sign
The self at peace: reliance on the other world, freedom from greed and sin
These are one self under three names, so changing attitude changes the name
Dhikr moves the self: the rest it gives is the peace of the third state
Fasting and night prayer loosen the same tie to the body
The soul takes habits quickly and whatever we make of it stays forever
Therefore what it becomes is in our hands

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Supplies the premise the whole section rests on: the soul is a microcosm, so senses, imagination and intellect each sample a world.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: First world via the senses; also plants 'unseen not because far away', which ¶7 needs.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Shows the imagination holds shape and colour without matter, the sample for the second world.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Names the world of images, establishes it exists independently of our minds, and states that the dead enter it.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Third world via the intellect: meaning without image or matter, inhabited by angels.

¶6.label: advance
¶6.why: Establishes the world of images as the middle term (barzakh); the point calls it 'the middle world' and ¶9 relies on this ordering.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: The key step: the worlds are dimensions of this one, nested in depth not distance. The closing sentence on kursi, arsh and jabarut is an aside inside an advancing paragraph and could go.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Draws the conclusion the point names: the dead have gone deeper, not away. Stated once, here.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Soul as intermediary between spirit and clay, hence sharing in all three worlds; gives the parallel with the world of images that ¶6 set up.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Attention held by the body keeps the soul in the witnessed world; announces the three loosenings the section will walk through.

¶11.label: advance
¶11.why: Sleep as the first loosening, with predictive dreams as the evidence that the soul reaches the middle world.

¶12.label: support
¶12.why: One-line lead-in to the verse pairing sleep and death, which ¶13 reads; carries no claim of its own.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Death as the second loosening: difference of degree from sleep, and the soul goes on in an image body.

¶14.label: support
¶14.why: Mostly re-says ¶13 (soul leaves body, continues in image body); the one new item, that the image body 'was with us all along', is what Section 3 (¶20, ¶26) needs to say the body is being shaped now. Could be cut to that sentence.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: Contemplation as the third loosening: same shift of attention achieved awake; defines muraqaba.

¶16.label: aside
¶16.why: Tabatabaʾi anecdote plus a caution that powers are not the aim. Illustrates ¶15 but nothing later uses it; the box already carries the Tabatabaʾi material. Cutting loses no step.

¶17.label: restate
¶17.why: First sentence summarises ¶11-¶15; second merely introduces the angel verse. The intro could be folded into ¶18.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Angels have fixed stations; the soul does not, so how far it goes is left to the life it lives. Closes the section's point.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Raises the objection the section answers and starts the answer with the habit mechanism (lying).

¶20.label: advance
¶20.why: Transfers the habit mechanism to the image body: sin deforms it, piety makes it shine. Core claim of the section.

¶21.label: support
¶21.why: Khomeini's authority for the unsourced claim in ¶20 that a second form is determined by the soul's qualities and fixed at departure; ¶26 leans on 'the form a soul meets after death'.

¶22.label: aside
¶22.why: Exists only to introduce the al-Nabaʾ verse that ¶23 reads; stands or falls with ¶23.

¶23.label: aside
¶23.why: A third authority for what ¶20-¶21 already established (people appear as they really are). The 'below a bug / above the angels' callback to Section 2 is attractive but no later sentence depends on it; ¶26 draws on ¶25, not here.

¶24.label: support
¶24.why: Introduces the al-Hadid verse on the light of the faithful, which ¶25 reads as 'piety makes it shine' and 'the light is their own'.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: New step: reward and punishment are the deeds themselves made manifest. ¶26 builds directly on this.

¶26.label: advance
¶26.why: Draws the conclusion: the form met after death is the deeds made visible, and it is being made today. First and only statement of the point's last clause.

¶27.label: advance
¶27.why: Links from Section 3 (self not fixed) and names the first state with its verse.

¶28.label: advance
¶28.why: Explains the commanding self: body overcoming spirit, including worry as a tie to the body. Reads the verse rather than leaving it bare.

¶29.label: advance
¶29.why: Names the second state and sets up its verse.

¶30.label: advance
¶30.why: Explains the self-blaming self and why it is hopeful; the point needs all three states defined.

¶31.label: advance
¶31.why: Third state, and the mechanism by which sustained self-blame leads to peace, which is the 'can move' part of the point.

¶32.label: advance
¶32.why: The three are one self under three names; because attitude can change, so can the state. Essential to the point.

¶33.label: aside
¶33.why: Amuli's four-state count is a second scholar on a settled step, adding a discrepancy the section then has to smooth over ('both counts describe one self climbing'). Nothing later uses it or the couplet.

¶34.label: advance
¶34.why: Turns to what moves the self and names dhikr first, with its verse.

¶35.label: support
¶35.why: Reads the al-Raʿd verse: the rest promised is the peace of the third state, so dhikr is the mover ¶34 announced. The remarks on sitting-still meditation and the Chapter Four callback are side matter within it.

¶36.label: advance
¶36.why: Fasting and night prayer as further movers, tied back to the body-loosening of Section 2.

¶37.label: advance
¶37.why: Why the acts work (soul takes habits quickly) and the point's key clause: whatever we make of the soul stays with us forever.

¶38.label: restate
¶38.why: Summarises the whole chapter (three worlds, sleep and death, deeds and form, three states) and repeats 'in our hands', which ¶37 has effectively delivered. A conclusion stated a second time.

¶39.label: aside
¶39.why: A one-line question pointing to the next chapter; raises something this section does not answer and supplies no step.
